title.zh: 卷七十一 列傳第一: 后妃
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第一: 后妃 Volume 71 Biographies 1: Emperesses and Consorts

sentences.zh: ○肅祖昭烈皇后蕭氏懿祖莊敬皇后蕭氏玄祖簡獻皇后蕭氏德祖宣簡皇后蕭氏太祖淳欽皇后述律氏太宗靖安皇后蕭氏世宗懷節皇后蕭氏世宗妃甄氏穆宗皇后蕭氏景宗睿知皇后蕭氏聖宗仁德皇后蕭氏聖宗欽哀皇后蕭氏興宗仁懿皇后蕭氏興宗貴妃蕭氏道宗宣懿皇后蕭氏道宗惠妃蕭氏天祚皇后蕭氏天祚德妃蕭氏天祚文妃蕭氏天祚元妃蕭氏

translations.literal: ○ Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Suzu; Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Yizu; Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xuanzu; Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Dezu; Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Emperor Taizu; Empress Jing'an of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Taizong; Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shizong; Consort Zhen of Emperor Shizong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Muzong; Empress Ruizhi of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Jingzong; Empress Rende of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong; Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong; Empress Renyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xingzong; Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xingzong; Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong; Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo; Virtuous Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo; Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo; Primary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan (Emperor Suzu); Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan (Emperor Yizu); Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan (Emperor Xuanzu); Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan (Emperor Dezu); Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan (Emperor Taizu); Empress Jing'an of the Xiao clan (Emperor Taizong); Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan (Emperor Shizong); Consort Zhen (Emperor Shizong); Empress of the Xiao clan (Emperor Muzong); Empress Ruizhi of the Xiao clan (Emperor Jingzong); Empress Rende of the Xiao clan (Emperor Shengzong); Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan (Emperor Shengzong); Empress Renyi of the Xiao clan (Emperor Xingzong); Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan (Emperor Xingzong); Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan (Emperor Daozong); Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan (Emperor Daozong); Empress of the Xiao clan (Emperor Tianzuo); Virtuous Consort of the Xiao clan (Emperor Tianzuo); Literary Consort of the Xiao clan (Emperor Tianzuo); Primary Consort of the Xiao clan (Emperor Tianzuo).

sentences.zh: 《書》始嬪虞，《詩》興《關雎》。

translations.literal: The Book begins with the consort of Yu; the Odes open with "Guanju."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents opens with the consort of Yu, and the Book of Odes begins with "Guanju."

sentences.zh: 國史記載，往往自家而國，以立天下之本。

translations.literal: National histories in their records often proceed from the family to the state, thereby establishing the foundation of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In recording national history, writers typically trace the line from household to state, thereby laying the foundation on which the realm rests.

sentences.zh: 然尊卑之分，不可易也。

translations.literal: Yet the distinction between superior and inferior cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the hierarchy of rank and station must not be overturned.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷列呂后於《紀》；

translations.literal: Sima Qian placed Empress Lü in the Annals;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian placed Empress Lü among the Annals;

sentences.zh: 班固因之，而傳元后於外戚之後；

translations.literal: Ban Gu followed him, yet placed the primary empress in a biography after the consort kin;
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu followed his example, yet placed the primary empress in a biography after the section on consort kin;

sentences.zh: 范曄登后妃於《帝紀》。

translations.literal: Fan Ye elevated empresses and consorts into the Imperial Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye placed empresses and consorts within the Imperial Annals.

sentences.zh: 天子紀年以敘事謂之《紀》，後曷為而紀之？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's chronicle by year for narrating events is called Annals—why then should empresses be entered in Annals?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's year-by-year narrative is called Annals—why, then, should empresses be recorded there?

sentences.zh: 自晉史列諸后以首《傳》，隋、唐以來，莫之能易也。

translations.literal: From the Jin History onward, all empresses were placed at the head of Biographies, and from Sui and Tang none could change this.
translations.idiomatic: From the History of Jin onward, all empresses were placed at the head of the Biographies, and from the Sui and Tang dynasties onward, no historian could alter the practice.

sentences.zh: 遼因突厥，稱皇后曰「可敦」，國語謂之「脦俚寋」，尊稱曰「耨斡{麻女}」，蓋以配后土而母之雲。

translations.literal: Liao, following the Turks, called the empress "Khatun"; in the national language this was "Teliyan"; the honorific title was "Nuwo," meaning, it is said, to pair with Queen Earth and be mother to all.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao, following Turkic usage, called the empress "Khatun"; in the Khitan language this was "Teliyan"; the honorific was "Nuwo"—said to pair her with Queen Earth as mother of the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱帝，尊祖母曰太皇太后，母曰皇太后，嬪曰皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu declared himself emperor, he honored his grandmother as Grand Empress Dowager, his mother as Empress Dowager, and his consort as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu declared himself emperor, he honored his grandmother as Grand Empress Dowager, his mother as Empress Dowager, and his primary consort as Empress.

sentences.zh: 等以徽稱，加以美號，質於隋、唐，文於故俗。

translations.literal: Ranks were set by honorific titles, fine epithets were added, substance drawn from Sui and Tang, ornament from former custom.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were graded by honorific designations and adorned with laudatory epithets—substance taken from Sui and Tang practice, phrasing drawn from older custom.

sentences.zh: 后族唯乙室、拔裏氏，而世任其國事。

translations.literal: The empress's clan were solely the Yishi and Baliji tribes, and for generations they held charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's kin came only from the Yishi and Baliji clans, and for generations they directed the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 太祖慕漢高皇帝，故耶律兼稱劉氏；

translations.literal: Taizu admired Emperor Gaozu of Han, and so the Yelü also took the surname Liu;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu admired Emperor Gaozu of Han, and so the Yelü clan also bore the surname Liu;

sentences.zh: 以乙室、拔裏比蕭相國，遂為蕭氏。

translations.literal: comparing the Yishi and Baliji to Chancellor Xiao, they thus became the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: likening the Yishi and Baliji to Chancellor Xiao of Han, they henceforth took the surname Xiao.

sentences.zh: 耶律儼、陳大任《遼史·后妃傳》，大同小異，酌取其當，著於篇。

translations.literal: The "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" in the History of Liao by Yelü Yi and Chen Daren agree in the main yet differ in small points; what is fitting has been selected and set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" in the histories compiled by Yelü Yi and Chen Daren agree in essentials yet differ in details; what is appropriate has been chosen and set down here.

sentences.zh: 肅祖昭烈皇后蕭氏，小字卓真。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Suzu, childhood name Zhuozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Suzu, whose childhood name was Zhuozhen.

sentences.zh: 歸肅祖，生四子，見《皇子表》。

translations.literal: She married Emperor Suzu and bore four sons, recorded in the Table of Imperial Sons.
translations.idiomatic: She married Emperor Suzu and bore four sons, as recorded in the Table of Imperial Sons.

sentences.zh: 乾統三年，追尊昭烈皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiantong, posthumously honored as Empress Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Qiantong era, she was posthumously honored as Empress Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 懿祖莊敬皇后蕭氏，小字牙裏辛。

translations.literal: Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Yizu, childhood name Yalixin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Yizu, whose childhood name was Yalixin.

sentences.zh: 肅祖嘗過其家曰：「同姓可結交，異姓可結婚。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzu once passed her home and said, "Those of the same surname may form friendships; those of different surnames may marry."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzu once passed her home and remarked, "Those who share a surname may be friends; those of different surnames may wed."

sentences.zh: 」知為蕭氏，為懿祖聘焉。

translations.literal: Learning she was of the Xiao clan, he betrothed her to Emperor Yizu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that she was of the Xiao clan, he arranged her betrothal to Emperor Yizu.

sentences.zh: 生男女七人。

translations.literal: She bore seven children, male and female.
translations.idiomatic: She bore seven children in all.

sentences.zh: 乾統三年，追尊莊敬皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiantong, posthumously honored as Empress Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Qiantong era, she was posthumously honored as Empress Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 玄祖簡獻皇后蕭氏，小字月裏朵。

translations.literal: Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xuanzu, childhood name Yueliduo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xuanzu, whose childhood name was Yueliduo.

sentences.zh: 玄祖為狠德所害，后嫠居，恐不免，命四子往依鄰家耶律臺押，乃獲安。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzu was killed by Hende; the empress lived as a widow, fearing she would not escape harm, and sent her four sons to rely on the neighbor Yelü Taiya, and thus found safety.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzu was murdered by Hende; the empress lived as a widow and feared she would not survive, so she sent her four sons to take refuge with their neighbor Yelü Taiya, and thus found safety.

sentences.zh: 太祖生，后以骨相異常，懼有陰圖害者，鞠之別帳。

translations.literal: When Taizu was born, the empress, because his bone structure was extraordinary, feared someone might plot against him in secret and reared him in a separate tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was born, the empress, seeing that his bone structure was extraordinary, feared secret plots against him and reared him in a separate tent.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，追尊簡獻皇后。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, posthumously honored as Empress Jianxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Chongxi era, she was posthumously honored as Empress Jianxian.

sentences.zh: 德祖宣簡皇后蕭氏，小字巖母斤。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Dezu, childhood name Yanmujin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Dezu, whose childhood name was Yanmujin.

sentences.zh: 遙輦氏宰相剔剌之女。

translations.literal: Daughter of Tila, chancellor of the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Tila, chancellor of the Yaolian clan.

sentences.zh: 男、女六人，太祖長子也。

translations.literal: She bore six children, male and female; Taizu was her eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: She bore six children; Taizu was her eldest son.

sentences.zh: 天顯八年崩，祔德陵。

translations.literal: She died in the eighth year of Tianxian and was enshrined at Deling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth year of the Tianxian era and was buried beside Emperor Dezu at Deling.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，追尊宣簡皇后。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, posthumously honored as Empress Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Chongxi era, she was posthumously honored as Empress Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 太祖淳欽皇后述律氏，諱平，小字月理朵。

translations.literal: Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Emperor Taizu, taboo name Ping, childhood name Yueliduo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Emperor Taizu, whose taboo name was Ping and childhood name Yueliduo.

sentences.zh: 其先回鶻人糯思，生魏寧舍利，魏寧生慎思梅裏，慎思生婆姑梅裏，婆姑娶勻德恝王女，生后於契丹右大部。

translations.literal: Her forebears: the Uyghur Nuosi, who begot Weining Sheli; Weining begot Shensimeili; Shensimeili begot Pagumeili; Pagumeili married a daughter of King Yundege and begot the empress in the Khitan Right Great Tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Her ancestors were Uyghur: Nuosi begot Weining Sheli; Weining begot Shensimeili; Shensimeili begot Pagumeili; Pagumeili married a daughter of King Yundege and the empress was born in the Khitan Right Great Tribe.

sentences.zh: 婆姑名月碗，仕遙輦氏為阿紥割只。

translations.literal: Pagumeili, named Yuewan, served the Yaolian clan as Azagachi.
translations.idiomatic: Pagumeili, whose name was Yuewan, served the Yaolian clan as Azagachi.

sentences.zh: 后簡重果斷，有雄略。

translations.literal: The empress was austere, weighty, resolute, and possessed bold strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was austere and resolute, with a bold strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 嘗至遼、土二河之會，有女子乘青牛車，倉卒避路，忽不見。

translations.literal: Once when she came to the confluence of the Liao and Tu Rivers, a woman riding in a green-ox cart hastily yielded the road and suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when she came to the confluence of the Liao and Tu Rivers, a woman riding in a green-ox cart hastily yielded the road and then vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，童謠曰：「青牛嫗，曾避路。

translations.literal: Before long a children's rhyme ran, "The Green-Ox Crone once yielded the road."
translations.idiomatic: Before long a children's rhyme circulated: "The Green-Ox Crone once yielded the road."

sentences.zh: 」蓋諺謂地祇為青牛嫗雲。

translations.literal: For in popular saying the earth spirit is called the Green-Ox Crone.
translations.idiomatic: In popular lore the earth spirit was called the Green-Ox Crone.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，群臣上尊號曰地皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the ministers submitted the honorific title Earth Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, his ministers submitted the honorific title Earth Empress.

sentences.zh: 神冊元年，大冊，加號應天大明地皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shence, at the great investiture, the title was augmented to Empress of Earth, Responsive to Heaven and Illustriously Bright.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shence era, at the grand investiture, her title was augmented to Empress of Earth, Responsive to Heaven and Illustriously Bright.

sentences.zh: 行兵禦眾，后嘗與謀。

translations.literal: In campaigning and controlling the masses, the empress often joined in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign and in commanding the armies, the empress often joined in planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗渡磧擊党項，黃頭、臭泊二室韋乘虛襲之；

translations.literal: Taizu once crossed the desert to strike the Tangut; the Huangtou and Choubo divisions of the Shiwei seized the moment to raid;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once crossed the desert to attack the Tangut; the Huangtou and Choubo divisions of the Shiwei seized the opportunity to raid the camp;

sentences.zh: 后知，勒兵以待，奮擊，大破之，名震諸夷。

translations.literal: the empress learned of it, marshaled troops to await them, struck fiercely, and routed them utterly; her fame shook all the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: the empress learned of it, marshaled the troops to meet them, struck fiercely, and routed them completely; her fame resounded among all the tribes.

sentences.zh: 時晉王李存勖欲結援，以叔母事后。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Li Cunxu wished to forge an alliance and addressed the empress as aunt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Cunxu, Prince of Jin, sought an alliance and addressed the empress as his aunt-by-marriage.

sentences.zh: 幽州劉守光遣韓延徽求援，不拜，太祖怒，留之，使牧馬。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang of Youzhou sent Han Yanhui to seek aid; he did not bow, Taizu was enraged, detained him, and set him to herd horses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang of Youzhou sent Han Yanhui to seek aid; Yanhui did not bow, and Taizu, enraged, detained him and set him to herd horses.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「守節不屈，賢者也，宜禮用之。

translations.literal: The empress said, "He kept his integrity and would not submit—a worthy man; he should be honored and employed."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "He held to his integrity and would not bow—a man of worth; he should be honored and put to use."

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃召延徽與語，大悅，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Taizu then summoned Yanhui to converse with him, was greatly pleased, and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then summoned Yanhui to speak with him, was greatly pleased, and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 吳主李掞獻猛火油，以水沃之愈熾。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu, Li Zhen, presented fierce fire-oil; when water was poured on it, it burned all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen, ruler of Wu, presented Greek fire; when water was poured on it, the flames burned all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 太祖選三萬騎以攻幽州，后曰：「豈有試油而攻人國者？

translations.literal: Taizu selected thirty thousand horsemen to attack Youzhou; the empress said, "Who would test oil and then assault another's state?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu selected thirty thousand horsemen to attack Youzhou; the empress said, "Would anyone test oil on a tree and then assault a whole kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 」指帳前樹曰：「無皮可以生乎？

translations.literal: She pointed to a tree before the tent and said, "Without bark, can it still live?"
translations.idiomatic: She pointed to a tree before the tent and asked, "Without its bark, can it still live?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Taizu said, "It cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "It cannot."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「幽州之有土有民，亦猶是耳。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Youzhou, with its land and its people, is just the same."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Youzhou, with its land and people, is just the same."

sentences.zh: 吾以三千騎掠其四野，不過數年，困而歸我矣，何必為此？

translations.literal: With three thousand horsemen I can raid its four borders; within a few years it will be exhausted and submit to us—why must we do this?
translations.idiomatic: "With three thousand horsemen I can harry its countryside; within a few years it will be worn down and come to us of its own accord—why take this risk?"

sentences.zh: 萬一不勝，為中國笑，吾部落不亦解體乎！

translations.literal: If by any chance we do not prevail, we will be laughed at by China, and will not our tribes also fall apart!
translations.idiomatic: "If we should fail, China will mock us, and our tribes will fall apart as well!"

sentences.zh: 」其平渤海，后與有謀。

translations.literal: In the pacification of Bohai, the empress shared in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Bohai, the empress shared in the planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，后稱制，攝軍國事。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, the empress assumed regency and directed military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, the empress assumed the regency and directed military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 及葬，欲以身殉，親戚百官力諫，因斷右腕納於柩。

translations.literal: At the burial she wished to follow him in death; kinsmen and officials urged her strongly, and she therefore severed her right wrist and placed it in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial she wished to follow him in death; kinsmen and officials pleaded with her, and she severed her right wrist and placed it in the coffin instead.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 會同初，上尊號曰廣德至仁昭烈崇簡應天皇太后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, the honorific title was submitted: Empress Dowager of Heaven, Broad in Virtue, Utmost in Benevolence, Illustrious and Liege, Lofty and Simple, Responsive to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huitong era, she was given the honorific Empress Dowager of Heaven, Broad in Virtue, Utmost in Benevolence, Illustrious and Liege, Lofty and Simple, Responsive to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖嘗謂太宗必興我家，后欲令皇太子倍避之，太祖冊倍為東丹王。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu had said that Taizong would surely revive our house; the empress wished the crown prince Bei to yield to him, and Taizu enfeoffed Bei as King of Dongdan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu had said that Taizong would surely revive their house; the empress wished the crown prince Bei to yield to him, and Taizu enfeoffed Bei as King of Dongdan.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，太宗立，東丹王避之唐。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Taizong was enthroned, and the King of Dongdan yielded the way and went to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, Taizong was enthroned, and the King of Dongdan withdrew to Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 太后常屬意於少子李胡。

translations.literal: The empress dowager often set her hopes on her younger son Li Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager often favored her younger son Li Hu.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，世宗即位於鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡以兵逆擊。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Shizong was enthroned at Zhenyang; the empress dowager was enraged and sent Li Hu with troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, Shizong was enthroned at Zhenyang; the empress dowager was furious and sent Li Hu with an army to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 李胡敗，太后親率師遇於潢河之橫渡。

translations.literal: Li Hu was defeated; the empress dowager personally led the army and met him at Hengdu on the Huang River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu was defeated; the empress dowager personally led her forces and met Shizong's army at Hengdu on the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 賴耶律屋質諫，罷兵。

translations.literal: Thanks to Yelü Wuzhi's remonstrance, the armies were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Yelü Wuzhi's remonstrance, both sides stood down.

sentences.zh: 遷太后於祖州。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was moved to Zuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was moved to Zuzhou.

sentences.zh: 應歷三年崩，年七十五，祔祖陵，謚曰貞烈。

translations.literal: She died in the third year of Yingli, aged seventy-five, was enshrined at Zuling, posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the third year of the Yingli era, at the age of seventy-five, was buried beside Taizu at Zuling, and was given the posthumous title Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Chongxi era, her posthumous title was revised to the present form.

sentences.zh: 世宗懷節皇后蕭氏，小字撒葛只，淳欽皇后弟阿古只之女。

translations.literal: Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shizong, childhood name Sagezhi, daughter of Agu of the younger brother of Empress Chunqin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shizong, whose childhood name was Sagezhi and who was the daughter of Agu, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 帝為永康王，納之，生景宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Yongkang, he took her in marriage; she bore Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still Prince of Yongkang, he took her as consort; she bore the future Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 天祿末，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianlu, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianlu era, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，生萌古公主。

translations.literal: The following autumn she bore Princess Menggu.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn she gave birth to Princess Menggu.

sentences.zh: 在蓐，察割作亂，弒太后及帝。

translations.literal: While still in childbed, Chage raised a rebellion and assassinated the empress dowager and the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: While she was still confined after childbirth, Chage rebelled and assassinated both the empress dowager and the emperor.

sentences.zh: 后乘步輦，直詣察割，請畢收殮。

translations.literal: The empress rode in a palanquin straight to Chage and begged that the burial rites be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress rode in a palanquin straight to Chage and begged that the dead be given proper burial.

sentences.zh: 明日遇害。

translations.literal: The next day she was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she too was murdered.

sentences.zh: 謚曰孝烈皇后。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Empress Xiaolie.
translations.idiomatic: Her posthumous title was Empress Xiaolie.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Chongxi era, her posthumous title was revised to the present form.

sentences.zh: 世宗妃甄氏，後唐宮人，有姿色。

translations.literal: Consort Zhen of Emperor Shizong, a palace woman of Later Tang, possessed beauty of form.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhen of Emperor Shizong was a palace woman of Later Tang, renowned for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 帝從太宗南征得之，寵遇甚厚，生寧王只沒。

translations.literal: The emperor obtained her on the southern campaign with Taizong; she received lavish favor and bore Prince Ning Zhimie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor obtained her on Taizong's southern campaign; she won his deep favor and bore Prince Ning Zhimie.

sentences.zh: 及即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 嚴明端重，風神閑雅。

translations.literal: Stern and bright, dignified and weighty; bearing serene and refined.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern and dignified, with a serene and refined bearing.

sentences.zh: 內治有法，莫幹以私。

translations.literal: In inner governance she had method; none could sway her with private interest.
translations.idiomatic: She governed the inner palace by strict rule, and no one could sway her with private appeals.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠、郭威稱帝，世宗承強盛之資，奄奄歲時。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei declared themselves emperors; Shizong inherited a position of great strength, yet the years dragged on feebly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei declared themselves emperors; Shizong inherited a powerful position, yet the years slipped by without decisive action.

sentences.zh: 后與參帷幄，密贊大謀，不果用。

translations.literal: The empress joined in the command tent, secretly supporting great plans, but they were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress joined him in council, secretly urging bold plans, but they were never carried out.

sentences.zh: 察割作亂，遇害。

translations.literal: When Chage rebelled, she was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chage rebelled, she was murdered.

sentences.zh: 景宗立，葬二后於醫巫閭山，建廟陵寢側。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, the two empresses were buried on Mount Yiwulu, and temples were built beside the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong took the throne, the two empresses were buried on Mount Yiwulu, with temples erected beside the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 穆宗皇后蕭氏，父知璠，內供奉翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Muzong; her father Zhifan was Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Muzong; her father Zhifan served as Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 后生，有雲氣馥郁久之。

translations.literal: At her birth, a rich cloud-aura lingered for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth, a rich cloudlike aura lingered for a long while.

sentences.zh: 幼有儀則。

translations.literal: In youth she had proper deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child she showed proper deportment.

sentences.zh: 帝居藩，納為妃。

translations.literal: While the emperor resided in his princedom, she was taken as consort.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still a prince, he took her as his consort.

sentences.zh: 及正位中宮，性柔婉，不能規正。

translations.literal: When she took the central palace, her nature was gentle and yielding; she could not correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Once she occupied the central palace, her gentle nature left her unable to correct the emperor's excesses.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: She had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no sons.

sentences.zh: 聖宗仁德皇后蕭氏，小字菩薩哥，睿知皇后弟隗因之女。

translations.literal: Empress Rende of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong, childhood name Pusage, daughter of Kuiyin, younger brother of Empress Ruizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Rende of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong, whose childhood name was Pusage and who was the daughter of Kuiyin, younger brother of Empress Ruizhi.

sentences.zh: 年十二，美而才，選入掖庭。

translations.literal: At twelve she was beautiful and talented and was selected for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twelve, beautiful and gifted, she was selected for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 統和十九年，冊為齊天皇后。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tonghe, she was invested as Empress Qitian.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Tonghe era, she was invested as Empress Qitian.

sentences.zh: 嘗以草莛為殿式，密付有司，令造清風、天祥、八方三殿。

translations.literal: Once she took a straw stalk as a model for a hall, secretly entrusted it to the relevant offices, and ordered the construction of the three halls Qingfeng, Tianxiang, and Bafang.
translations.idiomatic: Once she fashioned a straw model of a hall, secretly handed it to the works office, and ordered the construction of the Qingfeng, Tianxiang, and Bafang halls.

sentences.zh: 既成，益寵異。

translations.literal: When they were completed, she received still greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the halls were completed, she won still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 所乘車置龍首鴟尾，飾以黃金。

translations.literal: The carriage she rode was fitted with dragon head and owl tail, adorned with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Her carriage was fitted with a dragon head and owl tail, ornamented in gold.

sentences.zh: 又造九龍輅、諸子車，以白金為浮圖，各有巧思。

translations.literal: She also had built the Nine-Dragon carriage and the Princes' carriage, with pagodas of white gold, each showing ingenious design.
translations.idiomatic: She also commissioned the Nine-Dragon carriage and the Princes' carriage, each adorned with white-gold pagodas and showing ingenious craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 夏秋從行山谷間，花木如繡，車服相錯，人望之以為神仙。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn she followed on campaign through mountain valleys; flowers and trees like embroidery, carriages and robes intermingled—those who saw her took her for an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: In summer and autumn, as she traveled through mountain valleys where flowers bloomed like embroidery, her carriages and robes dazzling in procession, onlookers mistook her for a celestial being.

sentences.zh: 生皇子二，皆早卒。

translations.literal: She bore two imperial sons; both died young.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two imperial sons, but both died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 開泰五年，宮人耨斤生興宗，后養為子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai, the palace woman Noujin bore Xingzong; the empress reared him as her own son.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Kaitai era, the palace woman Noujin gave birth to Xingzong, whom the empress raised as her own son.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，耨斤詈后曰：「老物寵亦有既耶！

translations.literal: As the emperor grew gravely ill, Noujin reviled the empress, saying, "Does favor for an old creature never end?"
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay dying, Noujin reviled the empress: "Surely your days of favor must be numbered, you old woman!"

sentences.zh: 」左右扶后出。

translations.literal: Attendants on either side helped the empress out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants helped the empress withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，耨斤自立為皇太后，是為欽哀皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Noujin installed herself as empress dowager—this was Empress Qin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Noujin installed herself as empress dowager—she who would be known as Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 護衛馮家奴、喜孫等希旨，誣告北府宰相蕭浞卜、國舅蕭匹敵謀逆。

translations.literal: The guards Feng Jianu, Xisun, and others, seeking to please her, falsely accused the Northern Chancellor Xiao Pubu and the empress's brother-in-law Xiao Pidi of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The guards Feng Jianu and Xisun, eager to please her, falsely accused Northern Chancellor Xiao Pubu and the empress's brother-in-law Xiao Pidi of treason.

sentences.zh: 詔令鞫治，連及后。

translations.literal: An edict ordered investigation and trial, implicating the empress as well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their investigation, and the charges extended to the empress as well.

sentences.zh: 興宗聞之曰：「皇后侍先帝四十年，撫育眇躬，當為太后；

translations.literal: Xingzong, hearing of it, said, "The empress served the late emperor for forty years and reared my humble person—she ought to be empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzong heard of this, he said, "The empress served my late father for forty years and raised me from childhood—she ought to be empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 今不果，反罪之，可乎？

translations.literal: now that this cannot be, to turn and punish her—can that be right?"
translations.idiomatic: yet instead she is to be punished—how can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 」欽哀曰：「此人若在，恐為後患。

translations.literal: Qin'ai said, "If this person remains, I fear she will be a trouble afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai replied, "If she remains alive, she will surely become a threat later."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「皇后無子而老，雖在，無能為也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The empress has no sons and is old; though she remains, she can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The empress is childless and old—even if she lives on, she can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 」欽哀不從，遷后於上京。

translations.literal: Qin'ai would not agree and moved the empress to Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai would not relent and had the empress transferred to Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 車駕春蒐，欽哀慮帝懷鞠育恩，馳遣人加害。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went on the spring hunt, Qin'ai, fearing the emperor's gratitude for her nurturing, urgently sent men to do her harm.
translations.idiomatic: During the spring hunt, Qin'ai, fearing the emperor's gratitude for the empress's care in raising him, urgently dispatched assassins.

sentences.zh: 使至，后曰：「我實無辜，天下共知。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, the empress said, "I am truly innocent—all under Heaven knows it.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassins arrived, the empress said, "I am truly innocent, and all the realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 卿待我浴而後就死，可乎？

translations.literal: Will you wait until I have bathed and then accept death?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you wait until I have bathed before you kill me?"

sentences.zh: 」使者退。

translations.literal: The envoy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The assassins withdrew.

sentences.zh: 比反，后已崩，年五十。

translations.literal: By the time they returned, the empress had died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they returned, the empress was already dead, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 是日，若有見后於木葉山陰者，乘青蓋車，衛從甚嚴。

translations.literal: That day someone seemed to see the empress on the northern slope of Mount Muye, riding in a green-canopied carriage with a very strict escort.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, someone claimed to have seen the empress on the northern slope of Mount Muye, riding in a green-canopied carriage with a stately escort.

sentences.zh: 追尊仁德皇后。

translations.literal: She was posthumously honored as Empress Rende.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously honored as Empress Rende.

sentences.zh: 與欽哀並祔慶陵。

translations.literal: She was enshrined with Qin'ai at Qingling.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried beside Qin'ai at Qingling.

sentences.zh: 聖宗欽哀皇后蕭氏，小字耨斤，淳欽皇后弟阿古只五世孫。

translations.literal: Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong, childhood name Noujin, fifth-generation descendant of Agu, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Shengzong, whose childhood name was Noujin and who was a fifth-generation descendant of Agu, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 黝面狠視。

translations.literal: Dark of face, with a fierce gaze.
translations.idiomatic: She had a dark complexion and a fierce, piercing gaze.

sentences.zh: 母嘗夢金柱擎天，諸子欲上不能；

translations.literal: Her mother once dreamed of a golden pillar supporting Heaven; her sons wished to climb it but could not;
translations.idiomatic: Her mother once dreamed of a golden pillar supporting Heaven; her sons tried to climb it but could not;

sentences.zh: 後后至，與僕從皆升，異之。

translations.literal: when the future empress arrived, she and her attendants all ascended—her mother marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: when the future empress arrived, she and her attendants all ascended without difficulty—her mother took this as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 久之，入宮。

translations.literal: After a time she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In time she entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗拂承天太后榻，獲金雞，吞之，膚色光澤勝常。

translations.literal: Once while dusting the couch of Empress Dowager Chengtian, she found a golden rooster, swallowed it, and her complexion grew lustrous beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while dusting Empress Dowager Chengtian's couch, she found a golden rooster figurine, swallowed it, and her complexion grew unusually radiant.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「是必有奇子！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "She is sure to bear an extraordinary son!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager declared, "She is destined to bear an extraordinary son!"

sentences.zh: 」已而生興宗。

translations.literal: Soon afterward she bore Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she gave birth to Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 仁德皇后無子，取而養之如己出。

translations.literal: Empress Rende had no sons; she took him and reared him as if he were her own.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Rende, who had no sons of her own, took the child and raised him as her own.

sentences.zh: 后以興宗侍仁德皇后謹，不悅。

translations.literal: The empress was displeased that Xingzong attended Empress Rende with such dutiful care.
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai was displeased that Xingzong showed such dutiful devotion to Empress Rende.

sentences.zh: 聖宗崩，令馮家奴等誣仁德皇后與蕭浞卜、蕭匹敵等謀亂，徙上京，害之。

translations.literal: When Shengzong died, she had Feng Jianu and others falsely accuse Empress Rende, Xiao Pubu, Xiao Pidi, and others of plotting disorder; they were moved to Shangjing and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzong died, she had Feng Jianu and others falsely accuse Empress Rende, Xiao Pubu, Xiao Pidi, and others of treason; the empress was transferred to Shangjing and murdered.

sentences.zh: 自立為皇太后，攝政，以生辰為應聖節。

translations.literal: She installed herself as empress dowager and regent, making her birthday the Yingsheng Festival.
translations.idiomatic: She installed herself as empress dowager and assumed the regency, designating her birthday as the Yingsheng Festival.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，尊為仁慈聖善欽孝廣德安靖貞純寬厚崇覺儀天皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, she was honored as Empress Dowager of Heaven, Benevolent and Sagely, Dutiful and Filial, Broad in Virtue, Tranquil and Secure, Pure and Upright, Generous and Magnanimous, Lofty in Awareness, and Ceremonially Correct.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chongxi era, she was honored as Empress Dowager of Heaven, Benevolent and Sagely, Dutiful and Filial, Broad in Virtue, Tranquil and Secure, Pure and Upright, Generous and Magnanimous, Lofty in Awareness, and Ceremonially Correct.

sentences.zh: 三年，后陰召諸弟議，欲立少子重元。

translations.literal: In the third year, the empress dowager secretly summoned her younger brothers to counsel, wishing to establish her younger son Chongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, she secretly summoned her younger brothers to plot the installation of her younger son Chongyuan as heir.

sentences.zh: 重元以所謀白帝，帝收太后符璽，遷於慶州七括宮。

translations.literal: Chongyuan reported the plot to the emperor; the emperor seized the empress dowager's seals and moved her to Qiguo Palace in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyuan revealed the plot to the emperor, who seized the empress dowager's seals and confined her at Qiguo Palace in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，帝悔之，親馭奉迎，侍養益孝謹。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year the emperor regretted it, personally drove to welcome her back, and served her with still greater filial care.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year the emperor repented, personally went to fetch her back, and served her with redoubled filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 后常不懌。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was often displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager remained perpetually discontented.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，殊無戚容。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, she showed not the least grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, she showed not the slightest grief.

sentences.zh: 見崇聖皇后悲泣如禮，謂曰：「汝年尚幼，何哀痛如是！

translations.literal: Seeing Empress Chongsheng weeping in proper ritual, she said, "You are still young—why such bitter grief!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Empress Chongsheng weeping in proper mourning ritual, she said, "You are still young—why such extravagant grief!"

sentences.zh: 」清寧初，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingning era, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 崩，謚曰欽哀皇后。

translations.literal: She died; posthumous title Empress Qin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was given the posthumous title Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 后初攝政，追封曾祖為蘭陵郡王，父為齊國王，諸弟皆王之，雖漢五侯無以過。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager first assumed the regency, she posthumously enfeoffed her great-grandfather as Prince of Lanling, her father as King of Qi, and made all her younger brothers kings—even the Five Marquises of Han could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: When she first assumed the regency, she posthumously enfeoffed her great-grandfather as Prince of Lanling, her father as King of Qi, and made all her younger brothers kings—a favor even the Five Marquises of Han could not match.

sentences.zh: 興宗貴妃蕭氏，小字三蒨，駙馬都尉匹裏之女。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xingzong, childhood name Sanqian, daughter of the Commandant of Chariots Pili.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Xingzong, whose childhood name was Sanqian and who was the daughter of Commandant of Chariots Pili.

sentences.zh: 選入東宮。

translations.literal: She was selected for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was selected for the crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，以罪降貴妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi, for an offense she was demoted to imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongxi era, she was demoted to imperial consort on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 道宗宣懿皇后蕭氏，小字觀音，欽哀皇后弟樞密使惠之女。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong, childhood name Guanyin, daughter of Hui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and younger brother of Empress Qin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong, whose childhood name was Guanyin and who was the daughter of Hui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and younger brother of Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 姿容冠絕，工詩，善談論。

translations.literal: Her beauty surpassed all others; she was skilled in poetry and adept at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Her beauty was unrivaled; she was accomplished in poetry and skilled in conversation.

sentences.zh: 自制歌詞，尤善琵琶。

translations.literal: She composed her own song lyrics and was especially skilled at the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: She composed her own lyrics and was especially accomplished on the pipa.

sentences.zh: 重熙中，帝王燕趙，納為妃。

translations.literal: During Chongxi, when the emperor as prince feasted in Zhao, she was taken as consort.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi era, while the emperor was still prince on campaign in Zhao, he took her as consort.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，立為懿德皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, she was established as Empress Yide.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingning era, she was installed as Empress Yide.

sentences.zh: 皇太叔重元妻，以艷冶自矜，后見之，戒曰：「為貴家婦，何必如此！

translations.literal: The wife of the Imperial Grand Uncle Chongyuan prided herself on her seductive allure; when the empress saw her, she admonished her, saying, "As a woman of a noble house, why must you be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Imperial Grand Uncle Chongyuan prided herself on her seductive beauty; when the empress saw her, she admonished her: "As a woman of a noble house, why flaunt yourself so!"

sentences.zh: 」后生太子浚，有專房寵。

translations.literal: Later she bore Crown Prince Jun and enjoyed exclusive favor in his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later she bore Crown Prince Jun and enjoyed his exclusive favor.

sentences.zh: 好音樂，伶官趙惟一得侍左右。

translations.literal: She loved music; the performer Zhao Weiyi was allowed to attend at her side.
translations.idiomatic: She loved music, and the performer Zhao Weiyi was permitted to attend her constantly.

sentences.zh: 大康初，宮婢單登、教坊朱頂鶴誣后與惟一私，樞密使耶律乙辛以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, the palace maid Shan Deng and the Music Bureau's Zhu Dinghe falsely accused the empress of intimacy with Weiyi; Commissioner Yelü Yixin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dakang era, the palace maid Shan Deng and the Music Bureau performer Zhu Dinghe falsely accused the empress of an affair with Weiyi; Commissioner Yelü Yixin reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔乙辛與張孝傑劾狀，因而實之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yixin and Zhang Xiaojie to investigate and present findings, and thereby the charge was made to stick.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yixin and Zhang Xiaojie to investigate; they confirmed the false charges.

sentences.zh: 族誅惟一，賜后自盡，歸其屍於家。

translations.literal: Weiyi's clan was executed to the last; the empress was granted death by her own hand, and her body was returned to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyi's entire clan was executed; the empress was ordered to take her own life, and her body was returned to her family.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，追謚宣懿皇后，合葬慶陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong, posthumous title Empress Xuanyi was granted and she was buried with the emperor at Qingling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiantong era, she was posthumously honored as Empress Xuanyi and buried with the emperor at Qingling.

sentences.zh: 道宗惠妃蕭氏，小字坦思，駙馬都尉霞抹之妹。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong, childhood name Tansi, younger sister of Commandant of Chariots Xiamo.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Daozong, whose childhood name was Tansi and who was the younger sister of Commandant of Chariots Xiamo.

sentences.zh: 大康二年，乙辛譽之，選入掖庭，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dakang, Yixin praised her; she was selected for the rear palace and established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dakang era, Yixin recommended her; she was selected for the inner palace and installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，未見皇嗣。

translations.literal: After several years, no imperial heir appeared.
translations.idiomatic: After several years she had still not borne an heir.

sentences.zh: 后妹斡特懶先嫁乙辛子綏也，后以宜子言於帝，離婚，納宮中。

translations.literal: The empress's younger sister Wotelan had first married Yixin's son Suiye; the empress, citing her fitness to bear sons, spoke to the emperor, secured a divorce, and brought her into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's younger sister Wotelan had married Yixin's son Suiye; the empress told the emperor that her sister was fit to bear heirs, arranged a divorce, and brought her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 八年，皇孫延禧封梁王，降為惠妃，徙乾陵；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the imperial grandson Yanxi was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, she was demoted to Imperial Consort Hui and moved to Qianling;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the imperial grandson Yanxi was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, she was demoted to Imperial Consort Hui and sent to Qianling;

sentences.zh: 斡特懶還其家。

translations.literal: Wotelan was returned to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Wotelan was sent back to her family.

sentences.zh: 頃之，其母燕國夫人厭魅梁王，伏誅。

translations.literal: Before long, her mother, Lady of Yan, practiced sorcery against the Prince of Liang and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, her mother, the Lady of Yan, was found guilty of sorcery against the Prince of Liang and executed.

sentences.zh: 貶妃為庶人，幽於宜州，諸弟沒入興聖宮。

translations.literal: The consort was demoted to commoner, confined in Yizhou, and her younger brothers were seized into Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was demoted to commoner status, confined in Yizhou, and her younger brothers were seized and sent to Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 天慶六年，召還，封太皇太妃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianqing, she was summoned back and enfeoffed as Grand Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Tianqing era, she was summoned back and enfeoffed as Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 後二年，奔黑頂山，卒，葬太子山。

translations.literal: Two years later she fled to Mount Heiding, died, and was buried on Mount Taizi.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later she fled to Mount Heiding, where she died and was buried on Mount Taizi.

sentences.zh: 天祚皇后蕭氏，小字奪裏懶，宰相繼先五世孫。

translations.literal: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo, childhood name Duolilan, fifth-generation descendant of Chancellor Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo, whose childhood name was Duolilan and who was a fifth-generation descendant of Chancellor Jixian.

sentences.zh: 大安三年入宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the palace in the third year of the Da'an era.

sentences.zh: 明年，封燕國王妃。

translations.literal: The following year she was enfeoffed as Princess of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was enfeoffed as Princess of Yan.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong, she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiantong era, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 性閑淑，有儀則。

translations.literal: Her nature was gentle and virtuous; she had proper deportment.
translations.idiomatic: She was gentle and virtuous, with impeccable deportment.

sentences.zh: 兄弟奉先、保先等緣后寵柄任。

translations.literal: Her brothers Fengxian, Baoxian, and others, through the empress's favor, held power and office.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers Fengxian, Baoxian, and others wielded power through her favor.

sentences.zh: 女直亂，從天祚西狩，以疾崩。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen rebellion broke out, she followed Tianzuo on the western hunt and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen rebellion broke out, she accompanied Tianzuo on his flight westward and died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 天祚文妃蕭氏，小字瑟瑟，國舅大父房之女。

translations.literal: Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo, childhood name Sese, daughter of the Grandfather's House of the empress's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Emperor Tianzuo, whose childhood name was Sese and who was a daughter of the Grandfather's House of the empress's clan.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，帝幸耶律撻葛第，見而悅之，匿宮中數月。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong, the emperor visited the residence of Yelü Tage, saw her and was pleased, and concealed her in the palace for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiantong era, the emperor visited Yelü Tage's residence, saw her and was smitten, and kept her hidden in the palace for several months.

sentences.zh: 皇太叔和魯斡勸帝以禮選納，三年冬，立為文妃。

translations.literal: The Imperial Grand Uncle Heluwo urged the emperor to select and receive her according to ritual; in the winter of the third year she was established as Literary Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Grand Uncle Heluwo urged the emperor to take her according to proper ritual; in the winter of the third year she was installed as Literary Consort.

sentences.zh: 生蜀國公主、晉王敖盧斡，尤被寵幸。

translations.literal: She bore the Princess of Shu and Prince of Jin Aolugan, and was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Princess of Shu and Prince of Jin Aolugan, and enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 以柴冊，加號承翼。

translations.literal: By the firewood register, the additional title Chengyi was granted.
translations.idiomatic: According to the firewood register of succession, she was granted the additional title Chengyi.

sentences.zh: 善歌詩。

translations.literal: She was skilled at song and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in song and poetry.

sentences.zh: 女直亂作，日見侵迫。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen rebellion arose, daily she saw encroachment and pressure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen rebellion broke out, the realm faced daily encroachment and peril.

sentences.zh: 帝畋遊不恤，忠臣多被疏斥。

translations.literal: The emperor hunted and roamed without concern; many loyal ministers were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted and feasted without concern while many loyal ministers were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 妃作歌諷諫，其詞曰：「勿嗟塞上兮暗紅塵，勿傷多難兮畏夷人。

translations.literal: The consort composed a song of admonition; its words ran: "Do not sigh at the frontier's dim red dust; do not grieve at many hardships and fear the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The consort composed a song of admonition, which ran: "Do not sigh at the frontier's dim red dust; do not grieve at our hardships and fear the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 不如塞奸邪之路兮，選取賢臣。

translations.literal: Better to block the path of treacherous villains and select worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Better to block the path of treacherous villains and select worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 直須臥薪嘗膽兮，激壯士之捐身。

translations.literal: Only sleep on brushwood and taste gall to stir brave men to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Only sleep on brushwood and taste gall to stir brave men to sacrifice themselves.

sentences.zh: 可以朝清漠北兮，夕枕燕雲。

translations.literal: Then one may at dawn clear the northern desert and at dusk rest on the clouds of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Then at dawn you may clear the northern desert, and at dusk rest secure in the clouds of Yan."

sentences.zh: 」又歌曰：「丞相來朝兮劍佩鳴，千官側目兮寂無聲。

translations.literal: She sang again: "The chancellor comes to court—swords and girdle-pendants ring; a thousand officials turn their eyes—in utter silence.
translations.idiomatic: She sang again: "The chancellor comes to court—his sword and girdle ring; a thousand officials watch in silence.

sentences.zh: 養成外患兮嗟何及，禍盡忠臣兮罰不明。

translations.literal: Nurturing outer peril—alas, too late; calamity has consumed the loyal yet punishment is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: You nurtured outer peril—alas, too late; calamity has consumed the loyal yet punishment falls unclearly.

sentences.zh: 親戚並居兮藩屏位，私門潛畜兮爪牙兵。

translations.literal: Kinsmen all hold border-guard posts; private households secretly raise claw-and-fang troops.
translations.idiomatic: Your kinsmen hold every border post; private households secretly raise armies of their own.

sentences.zh: 可憐往代兮秦天子，猶向宮中兮望太平！

translations.literal: Pitiable—the Qin Son of Heaven of ages past still gazed from within the palace toward peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Pitiable—even the Qin emperor of old still gazed from his palace toward peace!"

sentences.zh: 」天祚見而銜之。

translations.literal: Tianzuo, seeing this, harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo, reading these songs, harbored deep resentment against her.

sentences.zh: 播遷以來，郡縣所失幾半，上頗有倦勤之意。

translations.literal: Since the flight into exile, nearly half the commanderies and counties had been lost; the emperor showed considerable weariness of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Since the flight into exile, nearly half the realm's commanderies and counties had been lost, and the emperor showed signs of weariness with his duties.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子敖盧斡最賢，素有人望。

translations.literal: Among the imperial sons, Aolugan was the most worthy and had long enjoyed popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Among the imperial sons, Aolugan was the most worthy and had long enjoyed the people's esteem.

sentences.zh: 元后兄蕭奉先深忌之，誣南軍都統余睹謀立晉王，以妃與聞，賜死。

translations.literal: The Primary Consort's elder brother Xiao Fengxian deeply resented him; he falsely accused the Southern Army Commander-in-Chief Yudu of plotting to install the Prince of Jin, implicated the consort as having known, and she was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Primary Consort's elder brother Xiao Fengxian deeply resented him; he falsely accused Southern Army Commander-in-Chief Yudu of plotting to install the Prince of Jin, claimed the Literary Consort had known of the plot, and she was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 論曰：遼以鞍馬為家，后妃往往長於射禦，軍旅田獵，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Commentary: Liao took saddle and horse as its home; empresses and consorts were often skilled in archery and horsemanship, and on military campaigns and hunts in the fields they were never absent.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Liao made saddle and horse their home; empresses and consorts were often skilled in archery and horsemanship, and on campaign and hunt they were never left behind.

sentences.zh: 如應天之奮擊室韋，承天之禦戎澶淵，仁懿之親破重元，古所未有，亦其俗也。

translations.literal: Such as Yingtian's fierce strike against the Shiwei, Chengtian's defense at Chanyuan, and Renyi's personal breaking of Chongyuan—unprecedented in antiquity, yet this was their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yingtian's fierce defeat of the Shiwei, Empress Chengtian's defense at Chanyuan, and Empress Renyi's personal suppression of Chongyuan's rebellion were unprecedented in history—yet such deeds were in keeping with Khitan custom.

sentences.zh: 靖安無毀無譽；

translations.literal: Jing'an had neither blame nor praise;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jing'an earned neither blame nor praise;

sentences.zh: 齊天巧思，乃奢侈之漸；

translations.literal: Qitian's ingenious designs were the first step toward extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qitian's ingenious designs marked the first step toward extravagance;

sentences.zh: 宣懿度曲知音，豈致誣蔑之階乎？

translations.literal: Xuanyi set tunes and knew music—how could this lead to the stage of false accusation?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi composed music and understood its art—how could that alone lead to false accusation?

sentences.zh: 文妃能歌詩諷諫，而謂謀私其子，非矣。

translations.literal: The Literary Consort could sing poems of admonition—yet to say she schemed for her son's private gain is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Consort sang poems of admonition—yet to claim she schemed on behalf of her son is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 若簡憲之艱危保孤，懷節之從容就義，雖烈丈夫何以過之。

translations.literal: Such as Jianxian's preserving the orphan through hardship and danger, and Huaijie's calmly accepting death for righteousness—even fierce husbands could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxian's preservation of the orphan through hardship and Huaijie's calm acceptance of death for righteousness—even the boldest of men could not surpass them.

sentences.zh: 欽哀狠桀，賊殺嫡後，而興宗不能防閑其母，惜哉！

translations.literal: Qin'ai was fierce and brutal, murdering the legitimate empress, yet Xingzong could not restrain his mother—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai was fierce and brutal, murdering the legitimate empress, yet Xingzong could not restrain his mother—a lamentable failure!
